title: South India's cotton yarn market steadies after prolonged decline
content:
South India's cotton yarn market is showing signs of stabilising after a prolonged decline, with traders believing prices have bottomed out.
Improved sentiment following easing geopolitical tensions and expectations of stronger domestic demand lifted buyer confidence.
While Tiruppur yarn prices fell further, Mumbai saw modest gains, and cotton prices remained steady amid tight private supplies.

title: India’s Gujarat state unveils new industrial policy
content:
India’s Gujarat state yesterday unveiled an industrial policy to attract investments worth ₹10 trillion in the next five years.
The policy offers 15-50 per cent incentives across sectors and has four pillars—investment and manufacturing; innovation and research; skill development and employment; and sustainability and inclusive growth.
It includes a comprehensive support framework for start-ups.

title: ICE cotton rises on weaker dollar, optimism from easing crude oil
content:
ICE cotton futures rebounded as a weaker US dollar, bargain buying and technical buying supported prices after recent losses.
July cotton settled at 73.43 cents per pound.
Falling crude oil prices improved sentiment by easing concerns over textile production costs.
Traders continued to monitor crop conditions, fund activity and geopolitical developments.

title: Chinese yarn glut bites Pakistan viscose; India, China hold
content:
The global viscose chain remained largely stable during the week, with Pakistan emerging as the only soft spot due to post-Eid destocking and a surge in low-cost Chinese yarn imports.
India’s pricing stayed steady amid predictable supply conditions, while China’s tight inventories and pre-sold output supported market stability despite weak downstream demand.

title: India's textile, apparel exports fall 4.4% in April-May
content:
India's textile and apparel exports fell 4.44 per cent year on year (YoY) to $5.91 billion in April-May FY27, dragged down by a 12.98 per cent decline in apparel shipments despite a 3.03 per cent rise in textile exports.
Weak Middle East demand and a high base impacted apparel export, while cotton imports surged and textile imports remained subdued.

title: India’s green manufacturing push: Solar farms to net zero
content:
Indian apparel manufacturers are embedding sustainability into factory design, energy sourcing and production processes to meet evolving global compliance requirements.
Investments in renewable energy, net-zero facilities and climate-resilient infrastructure are accelerating, while heat stress mitigation and decarbonisation are emerging as critical priorities for long-term competitiveness.
